rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods / Results (Figs 1-9) - laboratory incubation of two agricultural soils (loamy silt T1, sandy silt V1) at varying O2 partial pressures and moisture contents, measuring NO and N2O release by nitrification and denitrification with acetylene inhibition.
rows.notes: The study contains no irrigation treatment, no drip or subsurface drip system, and no crop yield data. It reports only that NO/N2O release by denitrification increases with decreasing O2 and increasing soil moisture, and that the fine-textured loamy silt showed higher N2O release by denitrification at 80-100% whc, which the authors assume indicates it became anoxic at a lower moisture content than the coarse-textured soil (Discussion, Fig. 6). This supports at most the precondition invoked in the passage (fine-textured soils have poorer aeration when wet), not the claimed effect on surface versus subsurface drip yield. The claim that coarse soils have poor water/nutrient holding capacity is not tested here either. Soil moisture was set by spraying water in serum bottles, not by any irrigation method.

notes: Study is a 1998 Global Change Biology paper (input lists 2004); full text appears complete. Pure laboratory soil microbiology study with no irrigation technology or crop production outcome.
